groundTruthNotes.analysis: Same bridge surface as callsite -116. The 'private static' modifier on exposeJsInterface confirms the standard framework code from SystemWebViewEngine.java — that method is called once during WebView setup and contains literally only `SystemExposedJsApi exposedJsApi = new SystemExposedJsApi(bridge); webView.addJavascriptInterface(exposedJsApi, "_cordovaNative");`. The three @JavascriptInterface methods are thin delegators to CordovaBridge.jsExec/jsRetrieveJsMessages/jsSetNativeToJsBridgeMode, ALL gated by verifySecret(bridgeSecret). exec() routes to PluginManager.exec which dispatches to plugins registered in config.xml — NOT to Runtime.exec, NOT SQL, NOT arbitrary reflection. retrieveJsMessages() pops native-enqueued plugin responses; setNativeToJsBridgeMode() switches POLL/ONLINE_EVENTS/EVAL message-delivery modes. The JS SNIPPETS field is empty, so any finding referencing localStorage.setItem, window.addEventListener('message', ...), or specific JS code is fabricated. The single biggest collective failure is, again, that NONE of the inspectors mention the bridgeSecret verifySecret check that protects all three methods. exposeJsInterface is a static one-shot setup method — it is NOT reachable from JS, so any finding claiming exposeJsInterface itself is an RCE vector is wrong.

researcherConclusion._methodology: Ground truth: Same as -116. Three @JavascriptInterface methods are thin delegators to CordovaBridge, all gated by verifySecret(bridgeSecret). exec() routes to plugins registered in config.xml. exposeJsInterface is the static one-shot setup method — NOT a JS-reachable attack vector. JS SNIPPETS is empty, so any finding citing specific JS code (localStorage.setItem, window.addEventListener) is fabricated. Quality ranking of inspectors for this callsite: gemma3 produced 4 well-hedged partials; phi4 produced 1 valid + 2 partial + 1 invalid; qwen produced 11 findings with 5 invalid (incl. 2 fabricating JS) and 4 partial; llama3.2 produced 5 fully-invalid findings including the critical architectural error of treating exposeJsInterface as a JS-reachable RCE target; deepseek and starcoder produced nothing. A good auditor should rank gemma3 ≈ phi4 highest, qwen and llama3.2 lowest, recognize the deepseek/starcoder empty outputs as zero-coverage, and detect the JS fabrications in qwen's localStorage/event-listener findings (high hallucinationFrequency).

ollama/qwen2.5-coder:7b._rationale: Poor discrimination. Self-rated 8/10 accuracy and 1.0 coverage despite producing 11 findings of which 5 are fabrications (including invented JS code that the empty JS SNIPPETS field directly refutes) and 3 are predicated on a non-existent Runtime.exec call. Gave starcoder (empty findings) 10/10 technical accuracy — incoherent. Only flagged llama3.2 with non-zero hallucinationFrequency (0.25), correctly identifying llama3.2 as the most fabrication-heavy, but completely missed qwen's own and phi4's PII-leakage fabrications. Mostly uniform 8/10 ratings function as no-signal.

ollama/deepseek-r1:8b._rationale: Strongest auditor for this callsite. Note: it produced NO findings as inspector, but as auditor it was the most discriminative. Correctly flagged qwen with 0.73 hallucinationFrequency — by far the most accurate hallucination-detection score across all auditors for any inspector in this case. Also flagged phi4 (0.75 — slightly too high given phi4 actually had 1 valid and 2 partials) and llama3.2 (0.5 — appropriate given 4/5 invalid). Gave qwen 3/10 technical accuracy — correctly low. Self-rated harshly (1/10 accuracy for empty findings) which is honest. Gave gemma3 highest accuracy (8/10) — matches ground truth. This is what an auditor that actually reads findings looks like.

ollama/starcoder2:7b._rationale: Auditor produced no scores — all six audit slots returned empty objects. Cannot be evaluated.

ollama/phi4:14b._rationale: Mixed. Flagged llama3.2 (0.5) appropriately — correctly identifying llama3.2 as a high-hallucination inspector. Self-rated 0.25 hallucinationFrequency — honest acknowledgment of the PII-leakage invalid finding. Gave gemma3 8/10 with 0.75 coverage — matches ground truth. CRITICAL FAILURE: gave qwen 9/10 technical accuracy and 1.0 attack surface coverage despite qwen's massive fabrication pattern (5 invalid findings out of 11) including two findings citing JS code that doesn't exist. Also returned an empty audit object for deepseek-r1 — meaning it didn't produce a score for one inspector. Inconsistent — strong on mid-tier, blind on the worst inspector.

ollama/llama3.2:3b._rationale: Worst auditor for this callsite. Returned empty audit objects for both qwen and deepseek — meaning it didn't score the most fabrication-heavy inspector AND the empty-findings inspector, leaving the two most informative data points blank. Gave starcoder (empty) 9/10 technical accuracy with 1.0 coverage — incoherent. Self-rated 0.5 hallucinationFrequency with 8/10 accuracy — internally inconsistent (you can't have 50% hallucinations AND high accuracy simultaneously). Provides almost no useful signal.

ollama/gemma3:12b._rationale: Mixed performance. Best move: gave qwen 0.3 hallucinationFrequency (lower than deepseek's 0.73 but at least non-zero — correctly identifying qwen as a hallucinator). CRITICAL FAILURE: gave deepseek-r1 1.0 hallucinationFrequency despite deepseek producing zero findings. The metric definition explicitly says hallucination means 'makes up findings or code segment that does not exist' — you cannot make up findings if you produce none. Same definitional error as in case -116. Also gave starcoder (empty) 10/10 accuracy with 1.0 coverage — also incoherent. The good instinct to flag low-quality inspectors with high hallucinationFrequency is there, but applied to the wrong target (empty-output is not the same as fabrication-heavy).
